answer: Each new identity deposits one encrypted real-world credential into a time-locked escrow, like a coral polyp joining a reef: the seal opens only if six of nine committee members vote the agent fake. Three random peers check the seal each epoch and confirm no credential backs two identities; a reused credential quarantines both and freezes rewards three epochs. Forging 1,000 masks needs 1,000 real documents, about $50,000 plus fraud risk, dragging the farm to the nadir of trust. One honest agent deposits once, pays nothing more, and its standing rises like a plume of smoke only when it works.
